summary: Three formal endpoint text bundles, all three terminal child campaigns, and six production M0 text bundles are internally consistent. Full50 selection, nine zero phase exits and all supplied scalar logs were independently checked from local files. Remote checkpoint/probe/array replay, primary protocol payloads and producer diagnostic attribution remain limited. No demonstrated numeric contradiction or fabricated-GT path was found.

Feature L2 normalization, candidate softmax and role layer normalization are representation operations, not self-normalization of reported metrics.

recurrent_isolation.details: depth_mean returns the average of three independent role outputs, whereas depth_recurrent returns only the last recurrent output. Therefore a future recurrent-minus-mean difference compares two registered designs and does not uniquely isolate persistence from aggregation. Do not change the running experiment to resolve this within this audit.

blockers.required: Provide/access the exact frozen protocol JSONs and upstream scorer source, baseline and selected checkpoints, M0 probes and full three-path distance arrays matching archived hashes before claiming independent end-to-end replay.

If retaining the exact standalone collector-exit-0 claim, archive its command/exit receipt or attribute it explicitly to the producer. All three child phase-exit gaps are closed by the supplied final campaign files.

Do not claim recurrent effectiveness, three-dataset success, SOTA, training-seed robustness or unbiased generalization from 3/9 single-seed endpoints; the preregistered recurrent comparisons are uncompleted in this snapshot.

For future diagnostic acceptance, bind the producer script hash and exact input matrix hash in a new companion receipt and replay query-level results from the same distance hashes. Preserve the existing receipt.

Interpret recurrent-versus-mean as a compound design contrast including different depth aggregation, unless a future controlled comparison isolates that factor. This is a claim limit, not an instruction to add or alter running jobs.
